meta.waveTitle: Make it a game — production, combat, an opponent, a result

now.title: Production — you cannot train a single unit
now.why: Played the build on device today and selected the Civilization Core: the command card did not change and there is no Train tile anywhere. Confirmed in source — SkirmishSimulation has no enqueue, no queue, no train. BuildingKind.trains exists and declares what each building makes; nothing reads it. SkirmishTuning.maxQueueLength and cancelRefundFraction exist; nothing reads either. Population is frozen at 4/8 for the whole match, which makes the Dwelling pointless and the Formation Yard unreachable. This is more basic than combat and it outranks everything else in the queue.
now.biggestGap: No production of any kind. The verb set is select, move, gather, build three of seven buildings.

next.title: Combat core
next.why: Sources/Simulation contains no CombatSystem. Units cannot attack, cannot take damage and cannot die, so the entire military half of an RTS is absent. Spec: Docs/Design/03-COMBAT-MODEL.md — deterministic, no damage variance, no miss chance, resolved in ascending EntityID order on the fixed 20 Hz tick.

next.title: Adversary v0
next.why: No AI of any kind exists in Sources/. Gravemark stands still for the entire match, so there is nothing to play against and no way to lose. A deterministic scheduled opponent — gather, train to 12, Formation Yard at 2:00, rising attack waves — is worth more than a clever one, because a player can learn to beat it.

next.title: Victory and defeat
next.why: The simulation has no way to end. The locked promise is two win paths in an 8-10 minute match: Conquest by destroying the enemy Core, and Dominion by holding the central Spire, with the hold requirement escalating at 8:00 and 10:00 so a match always resolves. Until this ships the honest answer to 'can a match be won or lost' is no.

log.title: Content design specification + bar changes BC-01 and BC-02
log.changed: Authored Docs/Design/ — 00-CONTENT-SPEC (principles, two tiers, faction split, victory), 01-UNIT-ROSTER (nine unit kinds, counter triangle, full stat and time-to-kill tables), 02-BUILDING-ROSTER (fourteen buildings, each unlocking something concrete, production model, two-page command grid), 03-COMBAT-MODEL (damage formula, armour classes, tick resolution, no RNG in combat at all), 04-IMPLEMENTATION-ORDER (nine checkpoints ranked by player-visible impact). Recorded the human's bar change from Age of Empires IV to Age of Empires II: The Rise of Rome in space as BC-01, and the demotion of performance to a guardrail as BC-02, both in 00-PLAN.md with old and new side by side.
log.taught: Writing the roster forced the arithmetic, and the arithmetic found the real state of the game: the implementation order I first drafted started with combat, and playing the build showed production is missing too — which is more basic. The order was rewritten before any of it was built.
log.next: Fresh critic on claude-opus-5-thinking-max reviews the spec before any roster content is implemented.

log.title: Construction — primary defect closed on device
log.changed: Ported the r2 worktree's fixes into the main tree by hand rather than merging, because the same files carry three other agents' in-flight work. The ghost now clears on a successful placement, camera gestures are re-enabled immediately after, refunds print exact fractions (+52.5 rather than 53), boarding and aboard citizens are excluded from builder assignment, builders per site are capped at four with diminishing returns, and a tap on an incomplete friendly foundation assigns builders to it.
log.taught: Two things. First, the fix is real and photographed: place a Farm and the ghost is gone, the camera works, the panel reads +52.5 Matter. Second, and more important — the previous entry's claim that ConstructionIntegrityTests ran 10 of 10 is NOT TRUE. That worktree's own IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md records that xcodebuild test was hook-blocked there, so no test executed. In this environment xcodebuild test runs but the app-hosted bundle dies at bootstrap because the host needs ~55 s to build its scene. No test in this repository has ever actually executed. P14 is in flight to fix that.
log.next: CP-G2a-prime after P14: audio, Reduced Motion, the full placement-state matrix, Matter Extractor and Dwelling completion.

log.title: Play report, second pass — five more dead controls
log.changed: Nothing. This is a play session.
log.taught: Beyond the missing production system: camera navigation does not exist except drag-pan. The minimap has no tap or drag gesture at all, and its four tool tiles — Face north, Go to Core, Place marker, Expand map — are HUDIconTile with a glyph, a name and no action. Six of the nine command tiles are the same: Move, Gather, Guard, Set rally point and Build Outpost all have action nil. Three buildings that exist as BuildingKind cases (Formation Yard, Expansion Outpost, Dawn Loom) have no tile and can never be built, which also makes the Voyager age unreachable. The resource rate readout prints +0 while the numbers climb.
log.next: CP-G2b-NAV for camera navigation; CP-G3a for production and the command grid.

log.title: Construction integrity — builders, cargo, refund
log.changed: Builder assignment excludes units that are boarding or aboard, carried resources have a defined disposition when a citizen starts construction, refunds report exact fractions, and stalled foundations can take builders again.
log.taught: The tests are runnable after all. A focused xctest run executed ConstructionIntegrityTests at 10 passed of 10 — which contradicts the standing claim in PROJECT_STATE.md that xcodebuild test is hook-blocked and no test has ever run.

log.title: Construction — Farm, Matter Extractor, Dwelling
log.changed: Command tiles with cost and purpose copy, full-footprint placement legality, a drag ghost, cost on commit, citizens constructing with linear multi-builder progress, cancellation refund, and a completion cue.
log.taught: An independent read-only review returned REVISE on a single defect the builder had not seen: after a successful placement the ghost stays on the new foundation, which immediately makes that footprint illegal, so the flow ends on a red BLOCKED state. A separate critic found in minutes what the builder had looked straight through.
log.next: Fix the post-place ghost state before anything else. Do not begin CP-G2b.

log.title: AoE land cut by void water
log.changed: Three map layouts — riverlands, basin, fjords — built from an authored land field with carved void bodies instead of unions of discs. The minimap contours the field; causeway decks span only the wet stretch. Land coverage 75.8 / 79.4 / 77.6 percent.
log.taught: Land coverage hit its target and the frame lost its art direction. Measured after the fact, void fell to 11% and then to 2.5% after the sparse retune, against concept 01's 53%, and the black point rose from 0.002 to 0.102 — the frame now contains no true blacks. The checkpoint passed because the measurement had quietly become land coverage instead of the concept comparison every checkpoint from CP-06 to CP-08 had used.
log.next: Piece P1 — restore void contrast at the play camera without giving up the continent.

proof.play: Captured on iPadOS 26.5, all three layouts

log.title: Contiguous land maps
log.changed: Overlapping plates replaced the separate land-blob pair; coastal docks; the opening camera moved onto interior land.
log.taught: The minimap still read as discs, which is what sent the work on to CP-14.

log.title: Mostly-land maps, neutral terrain, visual leftovers
log.changed: Void-heavy composition inverted to mostly land; a shared neutral land palette so fragments are never colour-coded by civilization; the Core plaza rosette, the pier lattice, stronger rim reach, and speed controls wired to the clock.
log.taught: Faction identity belongs on units, buildings, HUD and Core livery — not on the ground.

log.title: Transport and pier
log.changed: Removed the dark spar that read as a slab bolted to the docked transport — it was the unwoven causeway field sharing the transport's dock point — and added concept 01's gold lattice pier at the rim dock.
log.taught: This frame is still the closest the project has come to concept 01: 41.5% void, a 0.002 black point, the nebula and the gas giant in shot. It is the reference for what P1 has to get back to.

log.title: HUD parity
log.changed: Top-bar centre emblem and speed cluster, an alert strip, pinned group slots, selection portraits with life meters, and minimap silhouettes drawn from the real rim outline rather than ellipses.
log.taught: Four of concept 01's five chrome surfaces now match. The group slots are still chrome only, and the alert strip shipped with a seed cue that has never cleared since.

proof.play: Captured on iPadOS 26.5, with and without a selection

log.title: Rim, deposits and plant mass
log.changed: Pale crystalline rim spurs, larger lumen clusters, and tree-scale branching crowns where every prop had previously been a medium spiky clump.
log.taught: A new prop class was not enough — the canopy pass jammed against a scatter list already packed at 1.3 metres and almost nothing placed. Scatter density is capped by site spacing, not by candidate count.

log.title: The void
log.changed: Nebula wash, the celestial body actually inside the frustum, and drifting debris. Void floor luma 0.006 to 0.036 against the concept's 0.032; soft-void fraction 0.023 to 0.362 against 0.338.
log.taught: The celestial body was never missing — it was outside the frustum. Orthographic sky cards clip hard at about ±38.7 at default zoom, so anything authored beyond that simply is not in the frame.

log.title: The Core pavilion
log.changed: The closed dark dome became concept 01's tented pavilion. Canopy-to-ground luminance 0.57 to 1.13 against the concept's 1.15; Core box median 0.162 to 0.391 against 0.394; cold shadow 0.207 to 0.029.
log.taught: Two thirds of the fix was geometry, not albedo. Flattening the canopy droop from 36 to 20 degrees under a 52-degree key moved the ratio further than every albedo change put together. A surface's value is mostly a question of what it points at.

log.title: Density and palette
log.changed: 146 plantings against the concept's 132; bare-ground hue 42.2 to 32.7 degrees against the concept's 33.0; the periodic pit lattice removed from the sand.
log.taught: The 9-degree hue error was entirely in green, and it was on every lit surface at once including a near-white hull — so it was in the light, not the albedo. Rotating hue toward red costs exposure, because green carries 71% of luminance, and had to be repaid with exposureScale.

log.title: HUD chrome
log.changed: A live Canvas minimap drawn from WorldMap rather than a baked image, with the camera footprint as a yaw-rotated quad; a fixed 3×3 command grid where an inapplicable command dims in place rather than disappearing.
log.taught: A Spacer inside a SwiftUI column with no width of its own makes the whole column greedy — the minimap panel stretched the length of the frame instead of sitting in its corner.

proof.play: Captured on iPadOS 26.5, reticle verified under a real camera pan

log.title: Terrain relief
log.changed: Relief amplitude raised across the block and a TerrainSurface contract added so units, props, deposits and decals sit on the height field instead of on a datum plane.
log.taught: The terrain had been flat to hide a missing contract — groundHeight had exactly two callers, both inside the mesh factory, so nothing else in the project knew where the ground was. Also: a height-field grid sits above the function it samples, which is why the first render lost the gold seam network.

log.title: Make the light read
log.changed: Sunlit regolith 0.540 to 0.397 linear, landing exactly on concept 01. Frame over the bloom threshold 8.34% to 0.56%. Stars became soft points with a steepest single-pixel step of 0.12 instead of 0.62.
log.taught: Three defects that had been logged separately across two sessions were one number. Measuring the frame against the concept found it in one pass and turned the fix into arithmetic — the predicted regolith median was 0.397 and the render landed on 0.397. Measure the frame before theorising about the renderer.

log.title: Kill the magenta
log.changed: Fragment meshes tag faces with per-layer material indices but were being handed a single-element material array, so every face with index 1 or above resolved to no material. Placeholder-magenta pixels: 64,490 to 0.
log.taught: The material arrays are now built with allCases.map over the layer enums, so the array index is the emitted material index by construction rather than by a hand-kept parallel list that happens to be the right length today.

log.title: Green tree and honest baseline
log.changed: Restored a compiling tree carrying three independent mid-flight breaks in three files, each hidden behind the last, left by parallel agents that never re-verified together. Added build-agents/ to .gitignore, dropping git status from 35,602 lines to 21.
log.taught: A green build proves nothing about the frame. Three sessions of visual work had compiled cleanly while a third of the map rendered magenta, because no session had ever rendered the code. Every checkpoint since ends with an installed build and a full-resolution capture, or it does not close.
